notes: The reading: B, and PB5238's retirement stands on that point, but on 1985 grounds, not on its 24 red tests (tests verify, they do not decide). The 1985 text states the condition twice and differently: GR18 measures against "the record description entries for file-name-1"; IX.1.3.4 defines status 04 as a length that "does not conform to the fixed file attributes", and II.2.1 makes "the minimum and maximum logical record size" a fixed attribute "provided by the COBOL program", which the RECORD clause states (VII.3.8.1, GR3, GR4) and takes from the descriptions only when it omits them (GR1, GR6, GR7). Both readings survive GR18's words, so this is decided as latitude, and every other source points one way: Appendix B (informative) justifies 04 as a record "containing more or fewer characters than the maximum and minimum, respectively, specified for that file" and says it "cannot occur for records written by a program on an implementation of third Standard COBOL" because the WRITE refuses an out-of-range record (VII.3.8.4 GR10 measures integer-2/integer-3). Under reading A it occurs within one 1985 program (own probe ixsep: RECORD VARYING 4 TO 30 over one 12-character description, records of 6 and 30 written 00 and read back), so A contradicts the committee's statement; A would also make every short record of the RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON idiom over one maximum-size 01 a 04. §2023:14.9.30.4 GR14 keeps the same words with NOTE 2 reading them as the fixed-attribute check, and GnuCOBOL 3.2 measures against the file's record_min/record_max (RECORD clause widened by the descriptions). Under B the refuter's probes conform: r.cob (RECORD CONTAINS 30, one 20-character 01, a 30-character record) is inside the fixed attributes and 00 is right; r2.cob (VARYING 6 TO 30, a 9-character record) is inside, 00 with LEN 09 is right; ixsep gives 00/00/00. BUT the premise PB5238 and docs/CONFORMANCE.md rest on, that an indexed record outside the reader's attributes "cannot reach a READ", is false: KeyedConnector.FixedAttributeConflict validates nothing for a zero-byte store, so a connector opened INPUT on one, reading records another connector wrote afterwards under wider bounds, reads a 4- and a 20-character record under RECORD VARYING 5 TO 10 with status 00 (own probe ixzero; the reader's later OPEN gives 39, so the attributes do conflict). Those READs are outside the reader's own record size under either reading, so the rule requires 04, and the indexed READ has no 04 arm. PARTIAL, wrong-answer, silent. kb/Work PB5480 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set8/decisions.json (the adjudication of coderead-85/held-9.json, the 1985 read 4)).

next.reason: 1985 states for indexed files that a record shorter than the minimum leaves the rest of the record area undefined and a longer one is truncated on the right, READ successful with a length-conflict status. 2023 confines that text to 'For a record sequential file' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR14, which therefore states nothing for indexed files); for an indexed READ only the successful status 04 remains (§2023:9.1.13.2 GR3). The record-area content and truncation for an indexed file are no longer specified.
